content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 1 (as on 05.01.2026)
Key Insights

1. Rabi Sowing Status: As on January 02, 2026, the area sown under Rabi crops is 634.14 lakh ha (including 89.36 lakh ha in Rapeseed & Mustard & 95.88 lakh ha in Gram) as compared to 617.74 lakh ha during the corresponding period of last year.  As on 02.01.2026, 99% of area has been harvested for Kharif crops all over India. Approximately, 65.50% area of Pulses mainly in Uradbean (100%), Moongbean (100%) & Mothbean (100%); 98.18% area of Oilseeds majorly in Groundnut (100%), Soyabean (100%)& Sesamum (100%); 98.08% area of Shri Anna cum Coarse Cereals, majorly in Jowar (99.20%) & Bajra (98.87%) and 99% area of Rice has been harvested for crops of Kharif 2025-26. 2. Weather Update:
a) Temperature: Minimum temperatures are likely to be above normal in J&K, East

Rajasthan, Gujarat, South Karnataka, Rayalaseema, many parts of Tamil Ndu and many parts of NE India. TMIN is likely to be below normal in East India, Central India, many parts of NW India, many parts of Maharashtra, CAP, Telangana and Kerala. b) Rainfall Distribution: From January 01– January 04 2026, the All-India cumulative rainfall is 58% lower than its Long Period Average (LPA), with regional variations: (i) East & Northeast India: (-) 81%; (ii) Northwest India: (-) 58%; (iii) Central India: (-) 97%; and South Peninsula: 18%.  Subtropical westerly Jet Stream with core winds of the order of 130 knots at 12.6 km above mean sea level prevail over northwest India.  Isolated light/moderate rainfall/snowfall very likely over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit- Baltistan-Muzaffarabad during 5th -6th January; Himachal Pradesh on 5th & 6th January 2026, and Uttarakhand on 6th January 2026.  Ground frost very likely at isolated places over Uttarakhand on 5th & 6th January 2026.  Isolated rainfall activity likely over Western Himalayan Region, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Lakshadweep and Nicobar islands.  Dense to Very dense fog conditions very likely to continue during night/morning hours over North and adjoining central India during next 7 days.  Cold wave conditions very likely in isolated pockets of Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh during 5th -8th; over West Rajasthan during 5th -9th; over East Rajasthan during 5th -10th; over Jharkhand on 6th -7th January 2026.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 2 3. Inputs Situation a) Water Reservoir Status: As on 01 January 2026, the total live water storage in 166 important reservoirs across the country (monitored by CWC) is 142.177 billion cubic meter, which is 77.4% of total live storage capacity (183.565 BCM). The current year's storage is nearly 105.58 percent of last year's storage and 122.53 percent of the average storage of the last ten years during the corresponding period. The overall storage position is better than the corresponding period of last year in the country as a whole and is also better than the Normal storage during the corresponding period. b) Groundwater Levels: In August 2025, In Post-monsoon 2025, around 90% of the country's monitoring stations exhibited a depth to water level within 10 meters below ground level. Deeper water levels of more than 20 m are observed in around 5% of stations of the country covering mainly the western states, especially Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh.  The deeper groundwater level in the states like Western Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh during Post-monsoon 2025 has been significantly influenced by the over extraction of groundwater compared to the recharge during the monsoon period.  Annual water level comparison with the previous year Post-monsoon 2024 to Post- monsoon 2025 has shown that about 63% of total analyzed stations of the country experienced rise in annual water level fluctuation may be attributed to the less groundwater extraction compared to 2024.  About 73% of the analyzed stations of the unconfined aquifer experienced a rise of water level in the decadal mean water level fluctuation of 2015-2024 with respect to Post- monsoon 2025.  The Groundwater Drought Indices indicate that in Post-monsoon 2025, groundwater conditions across India remained largely stable, with 91% of monitoring stations showing no deficit. However, localized deficits were observed in several regions — notably in Meghalaya, Nagaland, and the Dadar Nagar Havili & Daman & Diu. c) Fertilizers: The fertilizer supply remains stable across all products.

content.text: Agricultural Statistics Division| Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare |Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare 4
Details of each Segment
1. RAINFALL

 During the week (25 Dec – 31 Dec 2025), lower rainfall was observed, as compared to Long Period Average (LPA) by 95%. Cumulative seasonal rainfall (01st Oct to 31 Dec 2025) is higher than LPA by 11%. Rainfall Forecast:  Overall, rainfall activity is likely to be below over the country except Tamil Nadu and Kerala, where it is likely to be near normal to above normal.
2. TEMPERATURE: MIN & MAX

Temerature Week 1 (02 Jan – 08 Jan 2026):  Minimum temperatures are likely to be below normal 2-4°C over most parts of the country except northeast India & Western Himalayan Region and many parts of northwest India, where these are likely to be above normal by 1-3°C during the week.

5. REMOTE SENSING BASED SOIL MOISTURE OBSERVATION

Soil Moisture Observation  Soil moisture during 26 Dec 2025 – 01 Jan 2026 is similar/better than the average of the past 9 years in major parts of M.P, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Haryana, Punjab, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Telangana, A.P. and Bihar.  It was lower than average of past 9 years in pockets of Odisha, West Bengal and N.E. part of the country.
